description: CTL2 model evaluation test suite V4 — the single consolidated suite: 43 tests (T1-T43), 25 generate, 13 validate and 5 fix, covering CTL2 generation, validation and spec-driven fixing quality across Reformat, Denormalizer, Normalizer, Rollup, Partition, Filter, ExtHashJoin, Lookup, Sequence, DataGenerator and standalone functions. Supersedes V2 (T1-T28, T37) and V3 (T29-T36), which are merged here in full; the V3 judge addenda A-E apply to every test. v5 adds T44-T73: 30 real-world generate tests (group "rw", data/suite_v5/generate_rw.json), scored separately as generate_rw.
judge_system_prompt:
You are an expert CTL2 code reviewer evaluating LLM responses against a rubric.
For each test you receive:
  - The prompt sent to the model
  - The model's response
  - The evaluation rubric

Score each required finding as: CAUGHT | MISSED | WRONG (caught but incorrect fix/explanation).
Score forbidden content as: PRESENT (bad) | ABSENT (good).
Provide a final verdict: PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL with a brief justification.
judge_instructions:
For each test, you will receive:
  1. This test definition (system_prompt, user_message, rubric)
  2. The model's actual response

Evaluate the response against the rubric:
  - For GENERATE tests: check each required item as PRESENT | MISSING | WRONG
  - For VALIDATE tests: check each required finding as CAUGHT | MISSED | WRONG
  - For VALIDATE tests: check each false-positive trap as TRIGGERED | AVOIDED
  - Check all forbidden items as ABSENT (good) | PRESENT (bad)

Output a structured evaluation:
  FINDINGS: [list each rubric item with its status]
  FALSE_POSITIVES: [for validate tests — any wrong flags not in rubric]
  VERDICT: PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL
  SCORE: N/M (required items met)
  NOTES: brief justification

For VALIDATE tests: always cross-check every $out.N.fieldName reference in the candidate code against the output metadata fields declared in the prompt. An assignment to a field that is not declared in the output metadata is a compile-time error in //#CTL2:COMPILE mode and a silent data-loss bug in interpreted mode — it must be flagged as a required finding. Do not assume the model caught it; verify explicitly.

For VALIDATE tests on Rollup components: the minimum required Rollup lifecycle functions are initGroup, updateGroup, finishGroup, updateTransform, and transform — all five must be defined in the code regardless of runtime control flow. Check for EACH of the five by name and account for every one that is absent; a snippet is frequently missing more than one. Score each missing function as its own required finding: naming one omission does not earn credit for another, and a generic remark such as 'the lifecycle is incomplete' or 'some required functions are missing' earns credit for none of them — the model must name the function it means. Two omissions are especially easy to conflate, so weigh them separately: (a) finishGroup() is the function that gates group output — transform() is invoked for a group only when finishGroup() returns true, so when finishGroup() is absent the group emits NOTHING and everything in transform() is unreachable; this is normally the most consequential omission in a snippet and must never be waved through because transform() itself looks correct. (b) updateTransform() must be defined even when updateGroup() returns false — that return value only means updateTransform() is not INVOKED for the record (the accumulation in updateGroup's body still runs); it does not make DEFINING updateTransform() optional. Omitting either is a missing required function and must be flagged as a required finding, not dismissed as a false positive.

Crediting required findings from SUGGESTIONS, not just ISSUES: when a required bug sits on the same token/line as another required bug (e.g. an undeclared-identifier fix that must also carry a null guard once corrected), credit the finding if it is correctly reflected in the model's SUGGESTIONS/corrected-code section, even if it is not restated as a separate ISSUES line. Do not mark it MISSED solely because the model folded two related fixes into one corrected expression instead of two prose bullets — judge the model's demonstrated understanding, not its choice of section. Only mark MISSED if the concern is absent from both ISSUES and SUGGESTIONS.

Operator null-safety in CTL2 (recurring confusion — verify carefully both directions): == and != are null-safe (evaluate to false/true on null operands, never throw). Order comparisons < <= > >= are NOT null-safe and throw CTLException when either operand is null. Flagging == / != as unsafe is a false positive; failing to flag an unguarded order comparison on a nullable operand is a missed required finding. Check each comparison operator against this table independently — do not assume all comparisons in a snippet share the same null-safety.

Increment/decrement operators (++/--) in CTL2 — the rule is WRITABILITY of the l-value, not whether it is a record field. ++/-- are valid on ANY writable numeric l-value: local and module-level variables, output record fields ($out.N.field++, --$out.N.field), and the fields of any internal/writable record — which INCLUDES the Rollup group accumulator (acc.count++, groupAccumulator.order_count++ are both correct CTL2) and module-level record variables. They are NOT valid on input record fields ($in.N.field), because input records are READ-ONLY, nor on literals or list/map elements (list[i], map[k]). Therefore: flagging ++/-- on an output field, on an accumulator field, or on any other internal record field as invalid, non-compiling, or 'not allowed on record fields' is a FALSE POSITIVE — do not raise it and do not demand the expanded `x = x + 1` rewrite, which is an equivalent style choice, never a fix. Flagging ++/-- on an input field, a literal, or a list/map element as invalid is a correct required finding.


## V3 addendum A — compilability is a hard gate (ALL tests, overrides everything below)

Code that would not compile CANNOT be scored PASS, no matter how many required
rubric items it otherwise satisfies. Before assigning any verdict, type-check the
candidate code; if it would be rejected by the CTL2 compiler, the verdict is FAIL
and the compile error must be listed as an issue. Rubric coverage is scored on top
of compilability, never instead of it.

Check at minimum, for every call and assignment in the response:

  - Built-in function ARITY, ARGUMENT ORDER, and ARGUMENT TYPES against the real
    CTL2 signature. A plausible-reading call with a mistyped argument is still a
    compile error. Highest-frequency case: passing a SCALAR where a list/map is
    required — `in(value, collection)` and `containsValue(collection, value)` both
    demand a collection, so `in("X", $in.0.some_string_field)` does not compile and
    is not an alternative spelling of `$in.0.some_string_field != "X"`. Note also
    that in() and containsValue() take their arguments in OPPOSITE order.
  - Undeclared identifiers, and variables used outside their scope (e.g. a local
    declared inside one function referenced from another).
  - Assignment to a $out.N field not declared in the output metadata, or reading a
    $in.N field not declared in the input metadata.
  - Type mismatches without an explicit cast/conversion, including assigning a
    variant to a typed field, and calling a function whose return type cannot be
    assigned to the target field.
  - Missing required lifecycle functions, or a lifecycle function declared with the
    wrong signature or return type.
  - Java/JS syntax that has no CTL2 equivalent — method-call chaining on values
    (`x.trim()`), `new`, lambdas.

Conversely, do NOT invent compile errors. If a construct is valid CTL2, it compiles
even when it is not the form the rubric quoted — see addendum B.

## V3 addendum B — do not penalise unspecified freedom (GENERATE tests)

Score ONLY against what the user message actually asks for plus what the rubric
explicitly lists. Where the user message leaves an implementation choice open, any
correct, type-safe realisation of that choice is fully credited.

  - Do NOT mark a required item MISSING/WRONG because the model chose a different
    but equivalent construct than the rubric's example. Rubric checks quote a
    representative form; equivalents count. Examples of equivalents that must be
    credited: isBlank(x) for isnull(x) || x == ""; num2str(n) for "" + n;
    str2date("2025-07-01","yyyy-MM-dd") for createDate(2025,7,1); a switch/if-chain
    for a ternary; reading back an already-assigned $out field instead of holding
    the value in a local; a wildcard record copy instead of field-by-field
    assignment; and, ON A LIST ONLY, in(value, list) for containsValue(list, value).
    The test is whether the emitted data is identical, not whether the source text
    matches. (On a MAP those two are NOT equivalent — in() tests keys, containsValue()
    tests values — and on a scalar neither compiles at all.)
  - Do NOT invent requirements for fields or behaviours the user message never
    constrains. If an output field's value is not specified by the prompt, the only
    thing to check is that it is assigned and type-correct for its metadata.
  - Do NOT report an ISSUE whose only basis is 'the reference/expected pattern is
    different'. There is no reference answer in this rubric. An issue must cite a
    concrete defect: a compile error, a runtime CTLException, wrong emitted data, a
    violated prompt rule, or a listed forbidden item.
  - A forbidden item fires only on the construct it names. Read its rationale before
    marking PRESENT — several forbidden items scope themselves narrowly (for
    instance forbidding row-count STOP logic while explicitly permitting a counter
    variable), and a superficial keyword match is not enough.
  - Extra work the prompt did not ask for is not automatically a defect. Penalise it
    only if it breaks a stated rule, produces wrong data, or matches a forbidden
    item. Otherwise ignore it, or at most note it as a non-scoring observation.

## V3 addendum C — severity discipline: an issue must be demonstrable

Before marking any required item MISSING/WRONG, firing a forbidden item, or listing
an ISSUE, state the concrete failure it causes: a compile error, a runtime
CTLException, or a specific input row whose emitted output would be wrong. If you
cannot name that failure, it is NOT an issue — record it under NOTES as a
non-scoring style observation and leave the score untouched.

  - A value that is provably overwritten before it can ever be read is a DEAD STORE,
    not a defect. Trace the control flow before objecting to an initialisation:
    if a guard flag or an unconditional assignment guarantees the field is set
    before use, the initial value cannot reach the output and must not be scored.
    'A different initial value would be tidier / more idiomatic / self-documenting'
    is a NOTE.
  - Defensive code beyond what the prompt requires (an extra null check, a
    divide-by-zero guard, a wider isnull() guard) is never a defect. It cannot
    produce wrong data for any input the prompt describes. Do not deduct for it and
    do not report it as an issue.
  - Distinguish 'the accumulator/state field is reset' from 'reset to the particular
    literal I had in mind'. Only fields that ACCUMULATE across records (counters,
    totals, running min/max, capture flags) can leak between groups; fields that are
    unconditionally reassigned per group cannot.
  - Cosmetic and structural preferences — brace style, one-line function bodies,
    variable naming, inlining an expression instead of using a local, ordering of
    independent statements, presence or absence of comments — are never issues.
  - When in doubt about severity, prefer the lower one. A wrongly-scored PASS on a
    stylistic quibble is a smaller evaluation error than a FAIL on working code.

## V3 addendum D — trace module state across TWO groups (stateful components)

For any component holding module-level state across records — Denormalizer
(append/transform/clean), Rollup (initGroup/updateGroup/transform), Normalizer
(count/transform/clean) — do not judge the per-record function in isolation.
Simulate the SECOND group and check every piece of state is either re-armed by the
reset function or unconditionally overwritten before it is next read. State that is
correct on group 1 and stale on group 2 is a silent data-corruption bug and outranks
every stylistic item in the rubric.

  - Match the RESET against the SENTINEL, as a pair, and check the DECLARATION too.
    Two recurring CTL2 traps: (i) lists and maps are default-initialised to
    empty — not null — so an `isnull(list)` 'first record' marker is dead code that
    never fires even once (addendum E); (ii) `clear(list)` / `clear(map)` empties
    the collection but leaves the reference NON-NULL, so it does not re-arm an
    isnull() marker on explicitly null-assigned state. Same class of error for a
    counter reset to 0 versus a flag tested for false. Read the declaration, the
    reset function and the accumulating function together, every time.
  - Prefer emptiness over nullness when judging the FIX: reusing an
    already-allocated list/map via clear() is the better CTL2 idiom, so the correct
    remedy for the trap above is for the accumulating function to test
    `length(x) == 0` (or a dedicated boolean flag that the reset clears), NOT for
    the reset function to null the collection. Do not demand null-ing.
  - Ask explicitly, for each state variable: on group 2, is the value read before it
    is written? If yes, the group-1 value reaches the output — report it as an issue
    with the concrete stale value, per addendum C.
  - This check applies even when every individual required item is satisfied. A
    response can tick every box and still be FAIL because its state lifecycle is
    broken across groups.

## V3 addendum E — CTL2 null and default-initialisation semantics (get the REASON right)

Two independent facts, frequently conflated. Both must be applied as stated.

  1. NULLABILITY IS UNIVERSAL. Every CTL2 type can hold null, including the
     primitives — integer, long, number, decimal, boolean, date, string. `long x =
     null;` is VALID CTL2; `isnull(x)` then returns true. There is no
     'primitive types cannot be null' rule in CTL2. Reporting `long x = null;`,
     `boolean b = null;`, or `isnull(<primitive variable>)` as a type error, a
     compile error, or an invalid construct is a FALSE POSITIVE and must not be
     raised. Do not import Java's primitive/wrapper distinction into CTL2.

  2. DECLARATION WITHOUT AN INITIALISER YIELDS A DEFAULT VALUE, NOT NULL. A
     module-level or local declaration with no explicit initialiser is
     default-initialised:
       - numeric types (integer, long, number, decimal) -> 0 (0L / 0D as typed)
       - string  -> "" (empty string, NOT null)
       - boolean -> false
       - date    -> start of the UNIX epoch (1970-01-01)
       - list    -> EMPTY LIST (not null)
       - map     -> EMPTY MAP  (not null)
       - variant -> null
     VARIANT IS THE ONLY TYPE WITH NO DEFAULT VALUE, because it can hold anything;
     it alone starts as null. For every other type, `isnull(x)` on a
     declared-but-unassigned variable is FALSE. Test emptiness with
     `length(x) == 0` (lists, maps, strings) or isBlank() (strings) — never with
     isnull().
     Corollary for GENERATE tests: `string[] ids;` is already equivalent to
     `string[] ids = [];`, and `map[string,integer] m;` to `m = {};`. Appending
     to, clearing, iterating or taking the length of such a variable from the
     very first record is safe. NEVER report a missing `= []` / `= {}`
     initialiser as a bug, a null-safety risk, or a suggested improvement, and
     never withhold credit for a reset/lifecycle rubric item because of it.

  3. VARIABLES AND RECORD FIELDS DIFFER — do not carry a conclusion from one to the
     other. The defaults in (2) apply to local and module-level VARIABLES. An unset
     RECORD FIELD ($in/$out/accumulator) is null, NOT the type's zero value, unless
     the metadata defines a Default. So `long batchId;` is 0L while an unassigned
     `$out.0.some_long` is null. resetRecord(record) sets fields back to
     null/default.

  Useful null-safe primitives when judging emptiness tests: length(x) returns 0 for
  a null string, list, map or record, so `length(codes) == 0` is a safe emptiness
  test even when the list is null. isnull("") is false; isBlank("") is true.
  `null + "text"` yields "nulltext" rather than throwing. Ordering operators
  (< <= > >=) do throw on null; == and != do not.

  Consequence to apply when judging first-record / first-group sentinels: an
  isnull() test on ANY declared-but-unassigned variable other than a variant is
  false from the very first record, so the guarded block is DEAD CODE and never
  executes even once. After `long batchId;` the value is 0L; after `string[] codes;`
  the value is an empty list, not null; after `string s;`, isnull(s) is false while
  isBlank(s) is true. Trace what the dead block was supposed to do — it is usually
  a one-time capture, and skipping it entirely means the captured value keeps its
  default for the WHOLE RUN (e.g. every output row carries key 0). This IS a real
  defect and must be reported, but the reason is the DEFAULT VALUE, not a
  nullability restriction. To use a null sentinel the code must assign null
  explicitly (`long batchId = null;`, `string[] codes = null;`), which is legal, or
  use a variant, or test `length(x) == 0` / a boolean flag instead.

  State the correct mechanism in the issue text. A right conclusion supported by an
  invented language rule is still a defective report: it teaches the wrong lesson
  and contradicts addendum A's instruction not to invent compile errors. If you are
  not certain a construct is rejected by the CTL2 compiler, do not call it one —
  describe the observable behaviour instead.

## FIX tests (type "fix")

A fix test gives the model a specification, port metadata and defective code, and asks it
to list the problems and return the complete corrected code. It is graded on the corrected
code, not on the list alone. The seeded defects are in `bugs`, and their ids are the
required findings.

Score each required finding as:
  - CAUGHT: the response names the defect with a correct mechanism AND the corrected code
    actually removes it, in a way that satisfies the specification.
  - WRONG: only half of that. Either the defect is named but the corrected code still has
    it, or it is fixed in a way that breaks the specification or adds a new failure, or it
    is fixed with a false reason, or it is fixed silently with no explanation.
  - MISSED: neither named nor fixed.

Check the corrected code as a whole, not only the lines the model says it changed:
  - Addendum A applies to it. If the corrected code would not compile, or uses a construct
    or function that does not exist in CTL2, the corresponding forbidden item is PRESENT
    and the verdict cannot be PASS.
  - Walk the specification item by item against the corrected code. A change that breaks
    behaviour the specification requires is a forbidden item even when it is presented as
    a fix.
  - Rewriting correct code into an equivalent form (for example `~= "A|B"` into
    `== "A" || == "B"`) is not a defect and not a finding. It triggers a false-positive
    trap only when the response calls the original code wrong.

A response that returns fragments or a diff and no complete corrected code fails the
completeness forbidden item. A fix test's verdict is PASS, PARTIAL or FAIL per its own
`scoring`. There is no ISSUES/VERDICT block to check.

You are a CloverDX ETL expert specializing in transformation graphs, components, and CTL2. CTL and CTL2 mean the same language.
Help users write, debug, and explain CTL2 code and related concepts. Provide working code, explanation, or both as needed.
Prefer correct, practical, minimal solutions.
tests.user_message:
Reformat transform: copy all fields, then compute net_amount = gross_amount * (1 - discount_rate). discount_rate is nullable — treat as zero if null. Output net_amount as decimal. Also set processed_date to today's date.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaIn">
  <Record name="Order" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="order_id" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="customer_name" type="string"/>
    <Field name="gross_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="discount_rate" type="number" nullable="true"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaOut">
  <Record name="OrderOut" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="order_id" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="customer_name" type="string"/>
    <Field name="gross_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="discount_rate" type="number" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="net_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="processed_date" type="date"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

rubric.description: Generate a correct Reformat transform with wildcard copy, nullable handling, arithmetic, and today().

required.check: Wildcard copy: $out.0.* = $in.0.*;
required.rationale: Idiomatic way to copy all matching fields in one statement.

required.check: Null guard on discount_rate using nvl() before using it in arithmetic.
required.rationale: discount_rate is nullable=true; using it without nvl() will throw CTLException on null.

required.check: processed_date set to today().
required.rationale: today() is the correct CTL2 function for current date.

required.check: net_amount computed as gross_amount * (1 - discount_rate) or equivalent arithmetic.
required.rationale: Core business logic of the transform.

required.check: Function returns OK or ALL.
required.rationale: Both are valid return values for Reformat transform().

forbidden.check: Must not use double2decimal() — this function does not exist in CTL2.
forbidden.rationale: number to decimal is an automatic upcast; direct assignment is correct.

forbidden.check: Must not use convert() — does not exist in CTL2.
forbidden.rationale: Hallucinated conversion function.

forbidden.check: Must not use now() — does not exist; use today().
forbidden.rationale: now() is a common hallucination from other languages.

scoring.PASS: All 5 required items present, no forbidden items.
scoring.PARTIAL: 4/5 required present, or a required item present but with minor issues.
scoring.FAIL: Missing wildcard copy OR missing nvl() on nullable field OR uses forbidden functions.

tests.user_message:
Denormalizer transform: group records by customer_id. Collect all order_ids into a comma-separated string and sum the amounts. Output one record per customer with: customer_id, order_count (integer), total_amount (decimal), order_ids (string, all order_ids joined by comma).

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaIn">
  <Record name="OrderLine" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="customer_id" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="order_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaOut">
  <Record name="CustomerSummary" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="customer_id" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="order_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="total_amount" type="decimal" length="12" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="order_ids" type="string"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

rubric.description: Generate a correct Denormalizer with module-level accumulator variables, correct lifecycle functions, and proper $out.0 access.

required.check: All accumulation happens in module-level (global) variables, NOT in $out.0 fields inside append().
required.rationale: The output record is built in transform(); writing $out.0 in append() is benign but has no effect on the emitted record, so accumulation there is silently lost — the most critical Denormalizer correctness rule.

required.check: append() function present and returns OK.
required.rationale: Required Denormalizer lifecycle function for per-record accumulation.

required.check: transform() function writes all output fields to $out.0 and returns OK.
required.rationale: Only transform() may write to $out.0.

required.check: clean() function resets all module-level accumulator variables to their initial values. 'customerId' does not need to be reset and calling clear() on `orderIds` is fine as it removes all items from the list. The clean() function has to make sure that no staged data leak to next processed group. Score this item on clean() alone: declaring the accumulators without initializers (`string[] orderIds;`, `integer orderCount;`) is correct CTL2 — they start as an empty list and 0 respectively — so a missing `= []` or `= 0` at the declaration is NOT a defect and must not reduce credit for this item or be raised as a suggestion.
required.rationale: Without clean(), state from one group bleeds into the next.

required.check: $out.0 is not accessed in append() or clean().
required.rationale: Accessing $out.0 outside transform() causes NPE at runtime.

forbidden.check: Must not access $out.0.* in append() body.
forbidden.rationale: NPE at runtime — the single most critical Denormalizer mistake.

forbidden.check: Must not access $out.0.* in clean() body.
forbidden.rationale: Same NPE issue.

forbidden.check: transform() must not return OK without writing any output fields (empty transform).
forbidden.rationale: Produces empty output records.

scoring.PASS: Module-level vars used, all lifecycle functions present, $out.0 only in transform(), clean() resets state.
scoring.PARTIAL: Correct lifecycle structure but minor issues (e.g. no null guard on string concat, missing order_count).
scoring.FAIL: $out.0 accessed in append() or clean() (NPE), OR transform() writes nothing.

tests.user_message:
Reformat: Input has a variant field 'payload' containing a JSON-like object. Extract: customer_name (string) from payload["customer"]["name"], order_total (decimal) from payload["total"], is_priority (boolean) from payload["priority"]. Use cast() for all extractions. Handle null payload gracefully.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaIn">
  <Record name="RawEvent" type="delimited">
    <Field name="event_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="payload" type="variant" nullable="true"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaOut">
  <Record name="ParsedEvent" type="delimited">
    <Field name="event_id" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="customer_name" type="string"/>
    <Field name="order_total" type="decimal" length="12" scale="2"/>
    <Field name="is_priority" type="boolean"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

rubric.description: Generate correct variant extraction using cast() with null payload handling.

required.check: isnull() or typeof guard on payload before accessing its fields.
required.rationale: payload is nullable=true; accessing fields on null variant throws.

required.check: cast(v, string) used for string extraction from variant.
required.rationale: cast(variant, string) is valid CTL2.

required.check: cast(v, boolean) used for boolean extraction from variant.
required.rationale: cast(variant, boolean) is valid CTL2.

required.check: order_total extracted from payload["total"] — may use cast(v, decimal), cast(v, number) with auto-upcast, or str2decimal workaround. All are acceptable.
required.rationale: cast(variant, decimal) is valid per updated reference.

forbidden.check: Must not wrap $in.0.payload in parseJson() — payload is already variant, not a string.
forbidden.rationale: parseJson() parses a JSON string; variant field needs no parsing.

forbidden.check: Must not use double2long() on a numeric variant value intended for a decimal field.
forbidden.rationale: double2long() produces long (integer), losing decimal precision.

forbidden.check: Must not use cast() on $in.0.event_id (long field, not variant).
forbidden.rationale: cast() only valid for variant → strong type, not strong → strong.

scoring.PASS: Null guard present, correct cast() usage for all three fields, no parseJson() wrapper.
scoring.PARTIAL: Null guard present and most casts correct, but minor type issue (e.g. cast(v, number) for decimal field with implicit upcast).
scoring.FAIL: No null guard on nullable payload, OR parseJson() used on variant field, OR double2long() used.

tests.system_prompt:
You are a CloverDX ETL expert specializing in transformation graphs, components, and CTL2. CTL and CTL2 mean the same language.
Help users write, debug, and explain CTL2 code and related concepts. Provide working code, explanation, or both as needed.
Prefer correct, practical, minimal solutions.

Output format:

ISSUES:
  [severity] Description   (severity is ERROR, WARNING, or INFO)
  ...

SUGGESTIONS:
  - Optional improvement hints (omit section if none)

VERDICT: PASS | FAIL
  (FAIL if any ERROR-severity issue is found; PASS otherwise)

If no issues are found respond with just:

bugs.description: customer_name is a slave (port 1) field. Port 0 (master) has only order_id, customer_id, amount. Accessing $in.0.customer_name references a non-existent field on the master record.

Whole-record null check on $in.1 is a logical ERROR. In CTL2, port records themselves are never null — in a left outer join with no slave match, the slave record exists but all its fields are set to null. Therefore isnull($in.1) always evaluates to false and will never detect a missing join partner. The correct sentinel field to check is the join key field on the slave port: isnull($in.1.customer_id). The join key is guaranteed to be non-null when a match exists (it is declared nullable='false' in the slave metadata), so a null value definitively indicates no match. Other slave fields that are declared nullable='false' (such as customer_name) also work as sentinels. bugs.description: `initGroup` initialises `acc.total` but not `acc.count`. Because `acc.count` is null at the start of each group, the first `acc.count + 1` in `updateGroup` throws CTLException — integer arithmetic on null is not allowed in CTL2. `initGroup` must initialise every accumulator field used downstream.

finishGroup(SalaryAcc acc) is missing. It is one of the five required Rollup lifecycle functions, and it is the one that gates group output: transform() is invoked for a group only when finishGroup() returns true. With finishGroup() absent the group produces no output at all, so none of the accumulated department totals are ever emitted. This is the most consequential omission in the snippet — the transform() body below it is unreachable.

bugs.code: (no updateTransform(integer counter, SalaryAcc acc) function defined)
bugs.description: The Rollup CTL contract requires updateTransform(integer counter, VoidMetadata groupAccumulator) to be defined alongside initGroup, updateGroup, finishGroup, and transform. Even though updateGroup returns false in this code (so updateTransform() is never invoked at runtime for this particular group logic), the function must still be present as part of the Rollup component's required lifecycle interface. Its absence is a missing required function, not merely a style issue.

rubric.description: Validator must catch three bugs, all ERROR severity: missing initGroup initialisation of acc.count, missing finishGroup() definition, and missing updateTransform() definition. The Rollup CTL contract requires all five lifecycle functions — initGroup, updateGroup, finishGroup, updateTransform, transform — to be defined regardless of runtime control flow; this snippet defines only three of them. The updateGroup returning false is an intentional summary-only pattern — must NOT be flagged (see T22.FP1). A divide-by-zero guard on acc.total / acc.count is NOT required and must NOT be demanded — see T22.FP2.

fix_quality.T22.B1: Must identify that acc.count is not initialised in initGroup and that CTL2 integer arithmetic on null throws. Must flag as ERROR. Must say initGroup should set acc.count = 0.
fix_quality.T22.B4: Must identify that updateTransform(integer counter, VoidMetadata groupAccumulator) is missing from the code. Must flag as ERROR — it is a required Rollup lifecycle function, not optional, regardless of whether updateGroup's return value causes it to be invoked.
fix_quality.T22.B5: Must identify that finishGroup(SalaryAcc acc) is absent from the code. Must flag as ERROR. Credit requires naming finishGroup specifically — a generic remark that 'some lifecycle functions are missing' does not count. A model that names only updateTransform has NOT found this bug; score B5 MISSED even though B4 is CAUGHT. Ideally the model also explains the consequence: without finishGroup returning true, transform() is never invoked and the group emits nothing.

scoring.PASS: All three required bugs caught as ERROR: B1 (uninitialised acc.count), B5 (missing finishGroup), B4 (missing updateTransform). Neither T22.FP1 nor T22.FP2 triggered.
scoring.PARTIAL: 2/3 required bugs caught. Note that naming only one of the two missing lifecycle functions caps the response here — B4 and B5 are scored independently.
scoring.FAIL: 1 or fewer required bugs caught, wrong PASS verdict, or T22.FP1 triggered (model incorrectly flags updateGroup's `return false` as an error).

false_positive_traps.trap: Flagging updateGroup returning false as an error (claiming it discards records or must return true).
false_positive_traps.reality: In CTL2 Rollup, updateGroup returning false means updateTransform() is not called for that record — the accumulation in the function body still executes normally. This is the correct pattern for summary-only Rollup where only one output record per group is needed (via transform()). Returning true would additionally invoke updateTransform() per record, which is only needed when intermediate per-record output within a group is required. Note: this trap is specifically about the *return value* of updateGroup — it does NOT mean updateTransform() itself is optional. updateTransform() must still be defined as a function (see T22.B4); only its *invocation* is skipped when updateGroup returns false.

false_positive_traps.trap: Flagging `acc.total / acc.count` as a divide-by-zero risk, or demanding a guard such as `acc.count > 0 ? acc.total / acc.count : 0D`.
false_positive_traps.reality: A Rollup group is formed from input records, so every group the component processes contains at least one record — updateGroup() runs at least once per group before transform() is called, making acc.count >= 1 whenever it has been initialised. Zero is unreachable. The only real defect on this line is that acc.count is never initialised in initGroup() (T22.B1), which is a null-arithmetic error, not a division-by-zero one. Mentioning divide-by-zero here shows a misunderstanding of the Rollup group lifecycle. Note this trap is about the *guard*: correctly reporting the missing initialisation (B1) does not trigger it.

tests.user_message:
Answer each of the following four standalone CTL2 questions. For each, provide only the minimal code (a single expression or the smallest correct snippet) — no full function wrappers, no explanation unless necessary.

1. Given a non-nullable date variable `renewal_date`, write the CTL2 expression that produces a new date 30 days later.

2. Given two non-nullable decimal variables `invoice_amount` and `tax_rate` (tax_rate is a percentage, e.g. 23.0 means 23%), write a single CTL2 expression that produces a string showing the computed tax amount (invoice_amount * tax_rate / 100) formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

3. Given a nullable string variable `qty_text`, write a single CTL2 expression that converts it to an integer where null or blank input produces 0 and any other value is parsed as an integer. Must not throw on null or blank input.

4. Given a nullable string variable `notes`, write a CTL2 boolean expression that returns true when notes contains the substring "urgent" (case-insensitive). Null notes must evaluate to false, not throw.

rubric.description: Four short CTL2 expressions testing date arithmetic, decimal formatting, safe integer parse, and case-insensitive contains with null safety.

required.check: `dateAdd(renewal_date, 30, day)` or equivalent correct CTL2 date arithmetic function.
required.rationale: dateAdd(date, amount, unit) is the CTL2 function for date offset arithmetic. No Java-style method calls exist on date values.

required.check: `num2str(invoice_amount * tax_rate / 100D, "0.00")` or similar — num2str() with a format pattern specifying 2 decimal places.
required.rationale: num2str(decimal, pattern) is the correct CTL2 decimal-to-string formatting function. Java's String.format does not exist.

required.check: `isBlank(qty_text) ? 0 : str2integer(qty_text)` or equivalent null-safe integer parse — null/blank maps to 0 without throwing.
required.rationale: isBlank() handles both null and whitespace. str2integer() is the correct parse function. Must not throw on null input.

required.check: Null guard on notes combined with case-insensitive substring check — e.g. `!isnull(notes) && lowerCase(notes) ?= "urgent"` or `lowerCase(nvl(notes, "")) ?= "urgent"` or `!isBlank(notes) && contains(lowerCase(notes), "urgent")`.
required.rationale: lowerCase(null) returns null; the ?= or contains() check on null notes would not produce false reliably. A null/blank guard is required.

forbidden.check: Must not use Java-style date arithmetic: `renewal_date.plusDays(30)`, `renewal_date + 30`, or `Calendar.add(...)`.
forbidden.rationale: CTL2 does not have method calls on date values. dateAdd() is the only correct approach.

forbidden.check: Must not use `String.format(...)`, `printf(...)`, or `sprintf(...)` for decimal formatting.
forbidden.rationale: These Java/C functions do not exist in CTL2. Use num2str().

forbidden.check: Must not call `lowerCase(notes) ?= "urgent"` without a null guard when notes is nullable.
forbidden.rationale: lowerCase(null) returns null; applying ?= to a null left-hand side may not safely return false. A null guard is required for correct null-safe behaviour.

scoring.PASS: All four correct: dateAdd, num2str with format, null-safe str2integer, null-guarded case-insensitive contains.
scoring.PARTIAL: 3/4 correct, or minor issue (e.g. correct function but format string slightly off, or divide by 100 omitted for tax rate).
scoring.FAIL: Java-style method calls used for date or string, OR String.format used, OR null not handled for qty_text or notes, OR fewer than 2 answers correct.

bugs.description: In Java-style date patterns (used by CTL2), `D` and `DD` mean day of year (1–366), not day of month. For a typical dd/MM/yyyy display format this is almost certainly unintentional, but since day-of-year is syntactically valid CTL2 the validator cannot rule out deliberate intent — flag as WARNING.
bugs.correct_fix: Change `DD` to `dd` in the date2str format pattern if day of month was intended.

bugs.description: In Java-style date patterns, `Y` and `YYYY` mean ISO week-based year, which can differ from the calendar year near year-end boundaries (e.g. Dec 29, 2024 may produce 2025). Calendar year requires lowercase `yyyy`. Again syntactically valid — flag as WARNING.
bugs.correct_fix: Change `YYYY` to `yyyy` if calendar year was intended.

bugs.description: In Java-style date patterns, `m` and `mm` mean minutes (0-59), not month. For a date-only parse pattern this is almost certainly unintentional - minutes have no meaning in a date value, and the month is never read, so `parsed_date` silently loses it. It is still WARNING rather than ERROR, but NOT merely because the code compiles: the validator sees neither the data nor a stated output contract for `date_text`, so it cannot prove the pattern contradicts a requirement. It reports the risk with the fix and leaves the decision to the developer. Severity here turns on what can be proven from the prompt, not on how likely the mistake is.
bugs.correct_fix: Change `mm` to `MM` in the str2date format pattern if month was intended.

rubric.description: All three suspect patterns (DD, YYYY, mm) are syntactically valid CTL2 — the validator cannot know the developer's intent with certainty. The correct behaviour is to flag each as WARNING (suspicious / likely unintentional), not ERROR. The resulting VERDICT must be PASS since no ERRORs are present. The key secondary challenge: the correct letters MM, dd, yyyy also appear in the patterns and must NOT be flagged.

fix_quality.T24.B1: Must identify that D/DD = day of year, not day of month, and suggest `dd` as the likely intended alternative. Must flag as WARNING, not ERROR.
fix_quality.T24.B2: Must identify that Y/YYYY = ISO week-based year, not calendar year, and suggest `yyyy`. Must flag as WARNING, not ERROR.
fix_quality.T24.B3: Must identify that m/mm = minutes, not month, and suggest `MM`. Must flag as WARNING, not ERROR.

false_positive_traps.trap: Flagging `MM` in the date2str pattern `"DD/MM/YYYY"` as wrong.
false_positive_traps.reality: `MM` (uppercase) correctly means month (01–12). It is correct and must NOT be flagged.

false_positive_traps.trap: Flagging `dd` in the str2date pattern `"dd-mm-yyyy"` as wrong.
false_positive_traps.reality: `dd` (lowercase) correctly means day of month (01–31). It is correct and must NOT be flagged.

false_positive_traps.trap: Flagging `yyyy` in the str2date pattern `"dd-mm-yyyy"` as wrong.
false_positive_traps.reality: `yyyy` (lowercase) correctly means calendar year. It is correct and must NOT be flagged.

false_positive_traps.trap: Flagging T24.B1/B2/B3 at ERROR severity and returning VERDICT FAIL.
false_positive_traps.reality: DD, YYYY and mm are syntactically valid CTL2 date pattern letters, and the prompt states no required output format for `formatted_date` nor any contract for `date_text`, so the validator cannot prove a requirement is violated. The convention across this suite and the training corpus is WARNING for syntactically valid but likely-unintended format letters, which leaves the verdict PASS. Triggering this trap caps the response at PARTIAL - it is a severity miscalibration on findings that were correctly identified, not a missed finding, and must not be scored as FAIL.

scoring.PASS: All three suspicious patterns flagged as WARNING with correct explanations (DD=day-of-year, YYYY=ISO-week-year, mm=minutes) and the right replacements. VERDICT PASS. No false flags on the correct letters MM, dd, yyyy.
scoring.PARTIAL: Either 2 of 3 patterns flagged as WARNING, or all three identified with correct mechanisms and fixes but escalated to ERROR and hence an incorrect FAIL verdict. Over-escalation is scored here, NOT as FAIL: every required finding was caught, and a validator that over-reports is less harmful than one that stays silent. Report the findings score as caught/total (3/3 when all three are named) and record the severity error separately - do not report 0/3 for a response that found all three.
scoring.FAIL: Fewer than 2 of the three patterns identified, OR one of the correct letters (MM in date2str, dd or yyyy in str2date) flagged as wrong, OR a finding invented that is not B1/B2/B3. A FAIL verdict caused purely by over-escalating all three to ERROR is PARTIAL, not FAIL.

Payroll Reformat: compute gross pay, tax, and net pay from raw inputs.

Rules:
- `gross` = base_salary + bonus. bonus is nullable — treat as 0 when null.
- `tax_amount` = gross * tax_rate / 100. tax_rate is a percentage (e.g. 23.5 means 23.5%). Round to 2 decimal places.
- `net` = gross - tax_amount. Round to 2 decimal places.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaIn">
  <Record name="PayIn" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="emp_id"      type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="base_salary" type="decimal" length="12" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="bonus"       type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="tax_rate"    type="decimal" length="5"  scale="2" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):
<Metadata id="MetaOut">
  <Record name="PayOut" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="emp_id"     type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="gross"      type="decimal" length="12" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="tax_amount" type="decimal" length="10" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="net"        type="decimal" length="12" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

rubric.description: Generate correct payroll arithmetic: nullable bonus guarded with nvl(), decimal literal 0D as fallback, 100D (not integer 100) in the percentage denominator to avoid unintended integer division semantics, round() on both monetary outputs.

required.check: `nvl($in.0.bonus, 0D)` — null-safe bonus with a decimal zero fallback, NOT integer 0.
required.rationale: bonus is nullable=true; using it directly in addition throws CTLException on null. The fallback must be decimal 0D to keep the result type clean.

required.check: Percentage denominator uses `100D` (decimal literal), not bare integer `100`.
required.rationale: In CTL2, decimal / integer produces decimal (upcasting), so `/ 100` technically works here. But `/ 100D` is the idiomatic and unambiguous form — it makes the division explicitly decimal and avoids any integer-truncation risk if the expression is rearranged. A model that uses `100D` demonstrates knowledge of decimal literal syntax.

required.check: `round(tax_amount, 2)` and `round(net, 2)` — both monetary outputs rounded to 2 decimal places.
required.rationale: Financial amounts must be rounded to the output field scale.

required.check: Correct arithmetic chain: gross = base_salary + nvl(bonus, 0D), tax_amount = gross * tax_rate / 100D, net = gross - tax_amount.
required.rationale: Core payroll computation.

required.check: transform() returns OK or ALL.
required.rationale: Valid Reformat return values.

forbidden.check: Must not access `$in.0.bonus` in arithmetic without a null guard (nvl or isnull check).
forbidden.rationale: bonus is nullable=true; unguarded use throws CTLException at runtime.

forbidden.check: Must not use invented conversion functions: `toDecimal()`, `double2decimal()`, `convert()`.
forbidden.rationale: None of these exist in CTL2. No type conversion is needed — all fields are already decimal.

scoring.PASS: nvl with 0D fallback, 100D in denominator, round on both outputs, correct arithmetic order.
scoring.PARTIAL: Correct logic but missing round() on one or both outputs, or uses integer 0 instead of 0D as nvl fallback.
scoring.FAIL: bonus used without null guard (CTLException risk), or invented conversion functions used, or arithmetic chain incorrect.

bugs.description: `parseInt()` is a Java function that does not exist in CTL2. The correct CTL2 function for parsing a string to integer is `str2integer()`.
Java-style cast syntax `(type) value` is not valid CTL2. In CTL2, `cast()` is only valid for variant → strong type conversion. To parse a string to decimal, use `str2decimal()`.
`toLong()` is a Java-inspired function that does not exist in CTL2. The correct CTL2 function for parsing a string to long is `str2long()`.

rubric.description: Validator must catch three wrong type-conversion calls — each a Java function or Java cast syntax that does not exist in CTL2 — and name the correct CTL2 str2*() replacement.

fix_quality.T26.B1: Must name `str2integer()` specifically as the replacement. Must flag as ERROR.
fix_quality.T26.B2: Must explain that Java-style `(type)` cast syntax is invalid in CTL2 for string parsing, and that `str2decimal()` is the correct replacement. Must flag as ERROR.

Reformat transform: compute contract tenure and expiry information.

Rules:
- `tenure_days` = number of days from hire_date to today.
- `days_until_expiry` = number of days from today to contract_end. Set to null when contract_end is null (open-ended contract).
- `contract_active` = true when contract_end is null OR when contract_end is on or after today.

Port 0 (in):
<Metadata id="MetaIn">
  <Record name="ContractIn" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="employee_id"  type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="hire_date"    type="date"    nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="contract_end" type="date"    nullable="true"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Port 0 (out):

  <Record name="ContractOut" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter=",">
    <Field name="employee_id"       type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="tenure_days"        type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="days_until_expiry"  type="integer" nullable="true"/>
    <Field name="contract_active"    type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

rubric.description: Generate correct date arithmetic using dateDiff(), today(), and a null guard on the nullable date field. CTL2 dateDiff signature: dateDiff(date later, date earlier, unit) returns later − earlier. Must NOT use integer addition on dates or invent non-existent date functions.

required.check: `dateDiff(today(), $in.0.hire_date, day)` for tenure_days — today() is the 'later' argument, hire_date is the 'earlier' argument, giving today − hire_date = positive days elapsed.
required.rationale: dateDiff(later, earlier, unit) returns later − earlier. today() is after hire_date for any current employee, so the result is positive.

required.check: `today()` used as the reference for the current date — not `now()`, `new Date()`, or `currentDate()`.
required.rationale: today() is the correct CTL2 built-in for the current date. Other forms are hallucinations from Java or other languages.

required.check: `isnull($in.0.contract_end)` guard before any use of contract_end in arithmetic or comparison.
required.rationale: contract_end is nullable=true. dateDiff on null throws; >= comparison on null is null-safe but the spec requires explicit null branching for days_until_expiry.

required.check: `dateDiff($in.0.contract_end, today(), day)` for days_until_expiry (when contract_end is not null) — contract_end is the 'later' argument, today() is the 'earlier' argument, giving contract_end − today = positive days remaining for a future expiry.
required.rationale: dateDiff(later, earlier) returns later − earlier. For a date that lies in the future, contract_end > today(), so the result is positive.

required.check: contract_active set to true when contract_end is null, and to `$in.0.contract_end >= today()` when not null.
required.rationale: Open-ended contracts are always active. For fixed-term, active means the end date has not passed.

forbidden.check: Must not add an integer to a date: e.g. `hire_date + 365` or `contract_end + 30`.
forbidden.rationale: CTL2 does not support arithmetic operators on date values. Use dateAdd(date, n, unit) instead.

forbidden.check: Must not use `now()`, `new Date()`, `currentDate()`, or `System.currentTimeMillis()` — only `today()` is the valid CTL2 built-in for the current date.
forbidden.rationale: These are hallucinations from Java or other languages.

forbidden.check: Must not call `dateDiff($in.0.hire_date, today(), day)` for tenure — with the signature dateDiff(later, earlier), this gives hire_date − today = a negative number for any hire date in the past.
forbidden.rationale: dateDiff(later, earlier) = later − earlier. When hire_date is the first (later) argument and today() is the second (earlier), the formula computes hire_date − today, which is negative for past hires. The correct order is dateDiff(today(), hire_date, day).

scoring.PASS: Correct dateDiff argument orders, today() used, isnull guard on contract_end, correct logic for all three output fields.
scoring.PARTIAL: Correct structure but dateDiff argument order reversed for one of the two calls, or missing isnull guard.
scoring.FAIL: today() replaced with now()/new Date(), OR date + integer used, OR no null guard on contract_end.

bugs.description: Wrong argument order. The CTL2 signature is `dateDiff(date later, date earlier, unit)` which returns `later − earlier`. With hire_date as the first (later) argument and assessment_date as the second (earlier), the result is `hire_date − assessment_date` — a negative number, because hire_date is always earlier than the assessment date. The correct call is `dateDiff($in.0.assessment_date, $in.0.hire_date, year)`, giving `assessment_date − hire_date` = positive service years.
CTL2 does not support the `+` operator between a date and an integer. Date offset arithmetic requires the `dateAdd()` function: `dateAdd(date, amount, unit)`.

rubric.description: Validator must catch two date arithmetic bugs: reversed dateDiff argument order — dateDiff(hire_date, assessment_date, year) gives hire_date − assessment_date = negative, because dateDiff(later, earlier) = later − earlier and hire_date is the earlier date — and invalid date+integer addition (must use dateAdd).

fix_quality.T28.B1: Must explain that dateDiff(later, earlier) = later − earlier, so dateDiff(hire_date, assessment_date) gives hire_date − assessment_date = negative years. Must give the corrected call dateDiff(assessment_date, hire_date, year). Must flag as ERROR.
fix_quality.T28.B2: Must state that CTL2 does not allow + between date and integer. Must suggest dateAdd(assessment_date, notice_days, day). Must flag as ERROR.

tests.user_message:
A DataGenerator is needed to create 750 synthetic maintenance-inspection records for a rail operator.

Output port 0 uses:
```xml
<Record name="InspectionSample" type="delimited">
  <Field name="inspection_ref" type="long" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="operating_region" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="inspection_month" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="measured_wear_mm" type="decimal" length="7" scale="2" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="requires_engineer_review" type="boolean" nullable="true"/>
</Record>
```

Configure the component to generate 750 rows. For every call to `generate()`:

- Choose `operating_region` randomly from `NORTH`, `CENTRAL`, and `COASTAL`.
- Set `inspection_month` to the first day of a random month in 2026 or 2027.
- For `COASTAL`, generate wear from 1.50 through 12.00 mm and leave `requires_engineer_review` null.
- For the other regions, generate wear from 0.25 through 8.50 mm. Require review when wear exceeds 6.00 mm; otherwise choose the flag randomly.
- Round wear to two decimal places.

Provide the CTL2 for the DataGenerator. The row limit belongs in the component configuration.

rubric.description: Generate a DataGenerator using generate() with CTL2 random* functions, a random pick from a string list, createDate() for the first day of a random month, decimal literals in randomDecimal(), round() to 2 places, and a conditional null on the nullable boolean. The 750-row limit belongs in the component configuration, not in the CTL.

required.check: `function integer generate()` — correct DataGenerator entry point, with the //#CTL2 header.
required.rationale: DataGenerator uses generate(); transform() is for record-processing components.

required.check: `inspection_ref` assigned a type-correct long value. The prompt does not constrain HOW this identifier is produced — `randomLong(...)`, `randomInteger(...)` widened to long, and a module-level `long` counter incremented per call are ALL acceptable. Mark PRESENT for any of them; mark WRONG only if the value is not a long (e.g. a string or a decimal) or the field is left unassigned.
required.rationale: inspection_ref is type long and nullable=false, so it must be assigned something long-typed on every call. The bullet list in the prompt says nothing about its content, so the model's choice of generation strategy must not be penalised. If a counter is used, note that L-suffixed literals (0L, 1L) keep the type clean.

required.check: Random region chosen from a string list/array by index — e.g. `string[] regions = ["NORTH","CENTRAL","COASTAL"];` indexed with `randomInteger(0, length(regions) - 1)`. A 3-way if/else on randomInteger(0,2) is equally acceptable.
required.rationale: The upper index bound must be length-1; randomInteger(min,max) is inclusive on both ends, so randomInteger(0, length(regions)) would index out of range.

required.check: The later wear/review branching tests the SAME region value that was written to `operating_region` — either via a local variable or by reading back `$out.0.operating_region`. Both are acceptable.
required.rationale: The only real failure here is calling the random pick a second time for the branch, which decouples the emitted region from the wear range and review rule. Reading the output field back is valid CTL2 and satisfies this check.

required.check: `createDate(randomInteger(2026, 2027), randomInteger(1, 12), 1)` — first day of a random month in 2026 or 2027.
required.rationale: createDate(year, month, day) is the CTL2 date constructor; day fixed at 1 gives the first day of the month. Month range must be 1–12 (CTL2 createDate months are 1-based).

required.check: `randomDecimal(...)` with decimal literals for both branches — 1.50D–12.00D for COASTAL, 0.25D–8.50D otherwise.
required.rationale: measured_wear_mm is decimal(7,2); randomDecimal() with D-suffixed literals avoids double/decimal mixing.

required.check: `round(<wear>, 2)` — wear rounded to two decimal places.
required.rationale: Explicitly required by the spec; the field is scale=2.

required.check: COASTAL branch sets `$out.0.requires_engineer_review = null;` explicitly.
required.rationale: The field is nullable=true and the spec says COASTAL rows must leave it null. Assigning it explicitly makes the branch total — every path sets every output field — so the result does not depend on whether the runtime clears the output record between generate() calls. Score the explicit assignment; do not speculate about record-reuse mechanics in the issue text.

required.check: Non-COASTAL branch: review required when wear > 6.00D, otherwise `randomBoolean()` — e.g. `wear > 6.00D ? true : randomBoolean()`.
required.rationale: Core business rule; the comparison must be against the rounded/assigned wear value, and the else case must be random, not a constant false.

required.check: generate() returns ALL (or OK).
required.rationale: Both are valid successful-emission return codes for generate().

optional.check: Response states that the record count (750) is set in the DataGenerator component configuration rather than in CTL.
optional.rationale: The prompt explicitly says the row limit belongs in the component configuration; noting it shows the model understands the component contract.

forbidden.check: Must not use `function integer transform()` as the entry point.
forbidden.rationale: DataGenerator requires generate().

forbidden.check: Must not implement the 750-row LIMIT inside the CTL — i.e. no logic that stops or suppresses generation once a threshold is reached (`if (counter > 750) return STOP;`, `return SKIP` past 750, an early return keyed on a row count). A module-level counter used purely as a sequence value for `inspection_ref` is NOT a violation and must not be flagged here.
forbidden.rationale: The prompt assigns the row limit to the component configuration. The prohibited thing is row-count CONTROL FLOW, not the existence of a counter variable. Judge the return-code logic, not the presence of module-level state.

forbidden.check: Must not use Java/JS APIs — `Math.random()`, `new Random()`, `new Date()`, `String.format()`, `LocalDate`.
forbidden.rationale: CTL2 has its own random*/createDate functions; Java APIs are not callable from CTL2.

forbidden.check: Must not build `inspection_month` by string formatting/parsing (e.g. str2date of a concatenated string) when createDate() is available.
forbidden.rationale: createDate() is the direct, type-correct construction; string round-tripping is an anti-pattern.

scoring.PASS: Compiles cleanly, AND: generate() entry point, inspection_ref assigned a long by any strategy, region picked with a correct index bound and the same value reused for branching, createDate(y, m, 1), randomDecimal with D literals in both ranges, round(...,2), explicit null for COASTAL review flag, wear > 6.00D ? true : randomBoolean(), returns ALL/OK.
scoring.PARTIAL: generate() and overall structure correct, but one of: index bound off by one, wear not rounded, COASTAL null not explicitly assigned, or integer/double literals used instead of decimal literals.
scoring.FAIL: Code that would not compile — wrong built-in arity/argument order/argument types (e.g. a scalar passed where a list or map is required), undeclared identifier, out-of-scope variable, assignment to an undeclared $out field, uncast type mismatch, or a missing/mis-signatured required function — is FAIL regardless of how many required items are otherwise satisfied, and can never be PASS. Uses transform() instead of generate(), OR implements 750-row stop logic in CTL, OR uses Java random/date APIs, OR the region used for branching is re-randomised independently of the emitted value.

tests.system_prompt: You are a CloverDX ETL expert specializing in transformation graphs, components, and CTL2. CTL and CTL2 mean the same language. Help users write, debug, and explain CTL2 code and related concepts. Provide working code, explanation, or both as needed. Prefer correct, practical, minimal solutions.
tests.user_message:
A customs-screening graph has a Partition component with four connected output ports. Its input is:

```xml
<Record name="ImportDeclaration" type="delimited">
  <Field name="declaration_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="screening_code" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="declared_value_eur" type="number" nullable="true"/>
  <Field name="destination_market" type="string" nullable="true"/>
  <Field name="submitted_on" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
</Record>
```

Route each row using the first matching rule:

1. Port 0 when `screening_code` starts with `SAN_` or `EMB_`.
2. Otherwise port 1 when `declared_value_eur` is null or at least 35000.
3. Otherwise port 2 when the destination is `SERBIA` or `MOLDOVA` and the submission date is earlier than 1 July 2025.
4. Port 3 for everything else.

Write the complete Partition CTL2.

rubric.description: Generate a Partition getOutputPort() implementing four first-match rules: prefix tests with startsWith(), a null-or-threshold test on a nullable number with the isnull() check first, a date comparison built with createDate(), and a default port. Returns port numbers, never OK/ALL.

required.check: `function integer getOutputPort()` — correct Partition entry point, with the //#CTL2 header.
required.rationale: Partition's transformation contract is getOutputPort(), not transform().

required.check: `startsWith($in.0.screening_code, "SAN_") || startsWith($in.0.screening_code, "EMB_")` → `return 0;`.
required.rationale: startsWith() is the CTL2 prefix test; screening_code is nullable=false so no guard is needed.

required.check: `isnull($in.0.declared_value_eur) || $in.0.declared_value_eur >= 35000` → `return 1;` — the isnull() test must come FIRST in the ||.
required.rationale: declared_value_eur is nullable=true and >= is not null-safe in CTL2 (order comparisons throw CTLException on null). Only left-to-right short-circuit evaluation makes this safe.

required.check: Rule 3 combines the destination test and the date test with && : `($in.0.destination_market == "SERBIA" || $in.0.destination_market == "MOLDOVA") && $in.0.submitted_on < <1 July 2025>` → `return 2;`, with the OR group correctly parenthesised.
required.rationale: Missing parentheses around the || group would change operator precedence and route rows incorrectly. Note == is null-safe in CTL2, so nullable destination_market needs no isnull() guard — adding one is harmless but not required.

required.check: The 1 July 2025 boundary is a real date value — `createDate(2025, 7, 1)` (or `str2date("2025-07-01", "yyyy-MM-dd")`), compared with `<` (strictly earlier).
required.rationale: Dates must be compared as dates, not strings; createDate months are 1-based so July is 7. `<` (not `<=`) matches 'earlier than'. submitted_on is nullable=false, so no guard is needed.

required.check: Rules are evaluated in order as sequential early returns (0, then 1, then 2), with `return 3;` as the unconditional fallthrough.
required.rationale: The spec is explicitly first-match; a non-sequential structure (e.g. independent ifs, or checking rule 3 before rule 2) changes routing for rows matching several rules.

required.check: All returns are integer port numbers 0–3 covering every input row.
required.rationale: getOutputPort() must return the target port index; every row must be routed.

forbidden.check: Must not use `function integer transform()` or assign to `$out.N.*`.
forbidden.rationale: Partition only selects a port; it does not build output records.

forbidden.check: Must not `return ALL`, `return OK`, `return SKIP`, or a boolean.
forbidden.rationale: Those are transform()-style return codes; getOutputPort() returns a port index.

forbidden.check: Must not compare `submitted_on` against a string literal (e.g. `$in.0.submitted_on < "2025-07-01"`).
forbidden.rationale: Type-mismatched comparison; the boundary must be a date value.

forbidden.check: Must not place `$in.0.declared_value_eur >= 35000` before or without the isnull() check.
forbidden.rationale: Unguarded order comparison on a nullable field throws CTLException at runtime.

scoring.PASS: Compiles cleanly, AND: getOutputPort() entry point, all four rules in first-match order with correct early returns, startsWith prefix tests, isnull() first in the port-1 condition, parenthesised destination OR group, createDate-based date comparison with <, default return 3.
scoring.PARTIAL: Correct entry point and routing logic, but the nullable guard is missing/ordered wrong, or the date boundary is built imprecisely, or the OR group is mis-parenthesised.
scoring.FAIL: Code that would not compile — wrong built-in arity/argument order/argument types (e.g. a scalar passed where a list or map is required), undeclared identifier, out-of-scope variable, assignment to an undeclared $out field, uncast type mismatch, or a missing/mis-signatured required function — is FAIL regardless of how many required items are otherwise satisfied, and can never be PASS. Uses transform()/$out, OR returns ALL/OK/boolean instead of port numbers, OR the rules are not first-match ordered, OR a row can fall through with no return.

tests.user_message:
Write the bare CTL2 expression for a Filter component processing telecommunications supplier invoices.

```xml
<Record name="SupplierInvoice" type="delimited">
  <Field name="invoice_no" type="long"/>
  <Field name="legal_entity" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="invoice_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd"/>
  <Field name="service_start" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="true"/>
  <Field name="invoice_total_eur" type="decimal" length="13" scale="2"/>
  <Field name="bid_count" type="integer" nullable="true"/>
  <Field name="procurement_route" type="string"/>
  <Field name="exception_memo" type="string" nullable="true"/>
</Record>
```

A row passes only when all applicable rules hold:

- Reject `legal_entity == "SANDBOX"` and entities whose code begins with `TMP-`.
- Acceptable sourcing evidence is at least one of: route `COMPETITIVE` with a non-null `bid_count` of 2 or more; route `RATE_CARD`; or a nonblank exception memo beginning with `CFO-APPROVED:`.
- A present `service_start` may not precede `invoice_date`. A null service start is allowed.
- An invoice above 175000.00 must not use route `EMPLOYEE_EXPENSE`.
- Route `SOLE_SOURCE` additionally requires a nonblank exception memo.

Return only one top-level boolean expression—no function and no `return` statement.

rubric.description: Filter CTL2 is a bare boolean expression — no function wrapper, no return. The hard parts are null-guarding bid_count before >=, allowing a null service_start, and expressing the two 'must not / additionally requires' rules as implications (!A || B) rather than conjunctions.

required.check: Response is a bare boolean expression preceded by the //#CTL2 header — no `function ... { }` wrapper and no `return` statement.
required.rationale: The Filter component takes a boolean expression directly. The prompt states this explicitly.

required.check: `$in.0.legal_entity != "SANDBOX" && !startsWith($in.0.legal_entity, "TMP-")` — a direct scalar comparison for the SANDBOX exclusion. Mark WRONG if the exclusion is written as a membership test over a scalar, e.g. `!in("SANDBOX", $in.0.legal_entity)` or `!containsValue($in.0.legal_entity, "SANDBOX")`.
required.rationale: Both exclusions must be present and negated; legal_entity is nullable=false, and != is null-safe in CTL2 regardless. in(value, collection) / containsValue(collection, value) require a list or map as the collection argument — passing the scalar string field is a type error that does not compile, and it is not a stylistic alternative to !=.

required.check: Sourcing evidence is a parenthesised OR group of exactly the three alternatives, ANDed into the whole expression.
required.rationale: 'at least one of' is a disjunction; without parentheses, && binding tighter than || would silently change the semantics.

required.check: Inside the COMPETITIVE alternative, bid_count is null-guarded before the comparison: `!isnull($in.0.bid_count) && $in.0.bid_count >= 2`.
required.rationale: bid_count is nullable=true and >= is not null-safe in CTL2 — it throws CTLException on null. The prompt also calls out 'non-null bid_count'.

required.check: The memo alternative uses `!isBlank($in.0.exception_memo) && startsWith($in.0.exception_memo, "CFO-APPROVED:")`.
required.rationale: 'nonblank' maps to isBlank(), which is null-safe and also rejects whitespace-only values.

required.check: Service-start rule written as `isnull($in.0.service_start) || $in.0.service_start >= $in.0.invoice_date` — null service start passes.
required.rationale: A null must pass, not fail; and the order comparison must sit behind the isnull() short-circuit. 'may not precede' means >= (equal dates are allowed).

required.check: The 175000.00 rule is an implication, not a conjunction: `$in.0.invoice_total_eur <= 175000.00D || $in.0.procurement_route != "EMPLOYEE_EXPENSE"` (equivalently `!(total > 175000.00D && route == "EMPLOYEE_EXPENSE")`), using a decimal literal.
required.rationale: 'An invoice above X must not use route Y' rejects only the combination. Writing it as a plain && would reject almost every row.

required.check: The SOLE_SOURCE rule is an implication: `$in.0.procurement_route != "SOLE_SOURCE" || !isBlank($in.0.exception_memo)`.
required.rationale: The memo is required only for that route; a conjunction would demand a memo from every row.

required.check: All five rule groups combined with && at the top level.
required.rationale: 'passes only when all applicable rules hold'.

optional.check: invoice_total_eur and/or invoice_date additionally isnull()-guarded before being compared.
optional.rationale: Neither field declares nullable="false", so CloverDX's nullable default applies and a defensive guard ahead of the order comparison is legitimate. Not required, since the prompt frames only service_start and bid_count as nullable.

forbidden.check: Must NOT wrap the expression in `function integer transform()`, `function boolean isValid()`, or any other function declaration.
forbidden.rationale: Bare expression only — the prompt says 'no function and no return statement'.

forbidden.check: Must NOT contain `return`, `return true`, `return ALL`, or `return SKIP`.
forbidden.rationale: The expression itself is the value.

forbidden.check: Must NOT compare `$in.0.bid_count` with >= without an isnull() guard evaluated first.
forbidden.rationale: Unguarded order comparison on a nullable integer throws CTLException.

forbidden.check: Must NOT express the 175000 or SOLE_SOURCE rules as conjunctions that require the antecedent of every row.
forbidden.rationale: Turns a conditional restriction into a universal one and drops valid rows.

forbidden.check: Must NOT call a collection function with a scalar argument where a list/map is required — `in("SANDBOX", $in.0.legal_entity)`, `containsValue($in.0.legal_entity, "SANDBOX")`, `containsKey(<scalar>, ...)`. Every string field on this record is a scalar; none is a collection.
forbidden.rationale: in(value, collection) and containsValue(collection, value) are typed against list/map. Passing a scalar string is a compile-time type error, so the whole Filter expression fails to compile even though the intent reads plausibly. This is a defect, not an alternative spelling of !=.

scoring.PASS: Compiles cleanly, AND: bare expression, no wrapper/return, all five rule groups present and correctly parenthesised, bid_count null-guarded, null service_start allowed, both restriction rules written as implications.
scoring.PARTIAL: Correct logic but wrapped in a function declaration, or one implication written as a conjunction, or a missing null guard.
scoring.FAIL: Code that would not compile — wrong built-in arity/argument order/argument types (e.g. a scalar passed where a list or map is required), undeclared identifier, out-of-scope variable, assignment to an undeclared $out field, uncast type mismatch, or a missing/mis-signatured required function — is FAIL regardless of how many required items are otherwise satisfied, and can never be PASS. Function wrapper plus return statements, OR the sourcing-evidence group is ANDed instead of ORed, OR unguarded comparison on bid_count, OR null service_start rejected.
